<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">operation and cash flow would be negatively impacted.&#160;&#160;Our credit losses have historically been within our expectations and the allowance established.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Inventory.</font>&#160;&#160;We state our inventories at the lower of cost or market, computed at standard cost on a first-in, first-out basis and market being determined as the lower of replacement cost or net realizable value.&#160;&#160;Inventory reserves are established when conditions indicate that the selling price could be less than cost due to physical deterioration, usage, obsolescence, reductions in estimated future demand and reductions in selling prices.&#160;&#160;Inventory reserves are measured as the difference between the cost of inventory and estimated market value.&#160;&#160;Inventory reserves are charged to cost of sales and establish a lower cost basis for the inventory.&#160;&#160;We balance the need to maintain strategic inventory levels with the risk of obsolescence due to changing technology, new product offerings and customer demand levels.&#160;&#160;Unfavorable changes in market conditions may result in a need for additional inventory reserves that could adversely impact our gross margins.&#160;&#160;Conversely, favorable changes in demand could result in higher gross margins.&#160;&#160;To date, actual reserve requirements have approximated management&#8217;s estimates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Goodwill and other intangible assets.</font>&#160;&#160;Effective January&#160;1, 2002, we adopted authoritative guidance issued by the FASB<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">,</font> which requires, among other things, the use of a nonamortization approach for purchased goodwill and certain intangibles.&#160;&#160;Under a nonamortization approach, goodwill and intangibles having an indefinite life are not amortized, but instead will be reviewed for impairment at least annually or earlier if an event occurs or circumstances indicate the carrying amount may be impaired.&#160;&#160;Events or circumstances that could indicate impairment include a significant change in the business climate, economic and industry trends, legal factors, negative operating performance indicators, significant competition, changes in our strategy or disposition of a reporting unit or a portion thereof.&#160;&#160;Goodwill impairment testing is performed at the reporting unit level.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2011, the FASB issued authoritative guidance in ASC 350, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Intangibles &#8211; Goodwill and Other</font> (&#8220;ASC 350&#8221;), with respect to the annual goodwill impairment test that adds a qualitative assessment which allows companies to determine whether they need to perform the two-step impairment test.&#160;&#160;We elected to adopt this accounting guidance early at the beginning of our third quarter of 2011 on a prospective basis for goodwill impairment tests.&#160;&#160;The guidance under ASC 350 gives an entity the option to first assess qualitative factors to determine whether the existence of events or circumstances leads to a determination that is more than likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount.&#160;&#160;If, after assessing the totality of events or circumstances, an entity determines it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, then the guidance requires that goodwill be tested for impairment using a two-step process.&#160;&#160;However, if an entity concludes otherwise, then it is not required to perform the two-step process.&#160;&#160;The first step of the goodwill impairment test, used to identify potential impairment, compares the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount, including goodwill.&#160;&#160;If the fair value of a reporting unit exceeds its carrying amount, goodwill of the reporting unit is not considered to be impaired and the second step of the impairment test is unnecessary.&#160;&#160;If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value, the second step of the goodwill impairment test must be performed to measure the amount of impairment loss, if any.&#160;&#160;The second step of the goodwill impairment test compares the implied fair value of reporting unit goodwill with the carrying amount of that goodwill.&#160;&#160;The implied fair value of goodwill is determined in the same manner as the amount of goodwill recognized in a business combination.&#160;&#160;If the carrying amount of the reporting unit goodwill exceeds the implied fair value of that goodwill, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Application of the goodwill impairment test requires judgment, including the identification of reporting units, assignment of assets and liabilities to such reporting units, assignment of goodwill to such reporting units, and determination of the fair value of each reporting unit.&#160;&#160;The fair value of each reporting unit is estimated using a discounted cash flow methodology.&#160;&#160;This requires significant judgments including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the long-term rate of growth for our business, the useful life over which cash flows will occur, and determination of our weighted average cost of capital.&#160;&#160;Changes in these estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and/or goodwill impairment for each reporting unit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have selected September&#160;30 as the date on which we perform our annual goodwill impairment assessment.&#160;&#160;We attribute the entire balance of our goodwill of $4.6 million to our largest operating segment, which is also a reporting unit, the physician-dispensed segment.&#160;&#160;We first performed the qualitative assessment to determine the need, if any, to perform the two-step impairment test, due to the following: (i) the historical significant excess of the fair value of our physician-dispensed reporting unit over its carrying value; (ii) our history of no impairment charges related to goodwill; (iii) our continued growth and the positive operating results of our physician-dispensed business; (iv) our brand recognition; and (v) our position as the market leader in the physician-dispensed channel.&#160;&#160;Our qualitative assessment of our physician-dispensed segment as of September 30, 2011 considered our current and projected operating results, our continued growth in spite of a slow-growth economy, current and future expected economic, market, and competitive conditions, and our current strategic initiatives.&#160;&#160;Based on our qualitative assessment, we determined that the fair value of our physician-dispensed segment continued to exceed the carrying amount of our goodwill by a significant </font></div>

<div align="left">&#160;</div>

<div align="left">
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">52</font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

</div>
</div>

<div align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">margin.&#160;&#160;As a result, we did not conduct the two-step impairment test on our goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;There were no impairment triggers subsequent to September 30, 2011 through the date of this annual report on Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;Based on our analyses, no goodwill impairment charges were recognized for the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009.<a name="eolPage43"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other intangible assets consist of trademarks, distribution rights, covenants not-to-compete, patents, customer lists, licenses and proprietary formulations.&#160;&#160;Other intangible assets are amortized over the expected period of benefit using the straight-line method over the following lives: trademarks (20&#160;years); distribution rights (ten years); covenants not-to-compete (seven years); and other intangible assets (three to 17&#160;years).&#160;&#160;In accordance with ASC 350, long-lived assets (including intangible assets that are amortized) are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable, such as a significant sustained change in the business climate, during the interim periods.&#160;&#160;If an indicator of impairment exists for any grouping of assets, an estimate of undiscounted future cash flows is compared to the asset group&#8217;s carrying value.&#160;&#160;If an asset is determined to be impaired, the loss is measured by the excess of the carrying amount of the asset over its fair value as determined by an estimate of discounted future cash flows.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In April 2011, the sublicensee of our non-exclusive right to market and sell any and all products marked under the &#8220;Obagi&#8221; brand containing a specific range of Kinetin concentration in Japan, ceased the manufacture and distribution of products containing the Kinetin concentration in February 2011.&#160;&#160;As a result, we recorded an impairment charge of $0.5 million during the three months ended March 31, 2011 related to the license.&#160;&#160;See Note 2 to our Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion.&#160;&#160;In addition, during the year ended December 31, 2011, we wrote off $0.4 million in patents that were abandoned.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There were no other indicators of impairment noted during 2011; therefore no other tests were performed for long-lived assets.&#160;&#160;Any unfavorable changes in market conditions or our product lines may result in the impairment of goodwill or an intangible asset, which could adversely impact our net income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Stock-based compensation.</font>&#160;&#160;We account for stock-based compensation in accordance with the guidance under ASC 718, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Compensation</font> (&#8220;ASC 718&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Determining the appropriate fair-value model and calculating the fair value of stock-based awards at the date of grant using any valuation model requires judgment.&#160;&#160;We use the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions.&#160;&#160;These assumptions include estimating the length of time employees will retain their stock options before exercising them (&#8220;expected term&#8221;), the estimated volatility of our common stock price over the expected term and the number of options that will ultimately not complete their vesting requirements (&#8220;forfeitures&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We estimated our options&#8217; expected terms in accordance with ASC 718, using our best estimate of the period of time from the grant date that we expect the options to remain outstanding.&#160;&#160;If we determine that another method to estimate expected volatility or expected term yields a more accurate estimate than our current methods, or if another method for calculating these input assumptions is prescribed by authoritative guidance, the fair value calculated for stock-based awards could change significantly.&#160;&#160;Higher volatility and expected terms result in an increase to stock-based compensation determined at the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The expected dividend rate and expected risk-free rate of return are not as significant to the calculation of fair value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Uncertainty in Income Taxes.</font>&#160;&#160;The provisions under ASC 740 prescribe a threshold for the financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return.&#160;&#160;Only tax positions meeting the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold at the effective date may be recognized or continue to be recognized upon adoption of this interpretation.&#160;&#160;The provisions also provide guidance on accounting for derecognition, interest and penalties, and classification and disclosure of matters related to uncertainty in income taxes.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, the liability for unrecognized tax benefits was $0.3&#160;million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<a name="FIS_RESULTS_OF_OPERATIONS"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net sales increased by $1.3&#160;million to $114.1&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $112.8&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Overall, we believe our net sales growth during the year ended December 31, 2011 was primarily due to the launch of new products, a larger base of active accounts and international physician-dispensed growth.&#160;&#160;However, we believe this growth was offset by the Texas regulatory matter (see &#8220;Overview&#8221; above for further discussion).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Physician-dispensed sales increased $1.3 million to $109.7 million during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $108.4 million during the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;We experienced net increases in the following product categories: (i) an increase in the Other category of $1.3 million; (ii) a $0.9 million increase in Nu-Derm sales; and (iii) an increase in Vitamin C of $0.2 million.&#160;&#160;The growth in the Other category was primarily attributable to the launch of Blue Peel RADIANCE in January 2011, which contributed $1.6 million, partially offset by $0.2 million in sales returns related to Texas.&#160;&#160;The growth in our Nu-Derm sales was primarily due to the launch of Nu-Derm Sun Shield SPF 50 in January 2011, which contributed $2.6 million; partially offset by $1.1 million in sales returns related to Texas. These product category increases were partially offset by: (i) a decrease of $0.8 million in the Therapeutic category; and (ii) a decrease of $0.2 million in Elasticity sales.&#160;&#160;The decline in the Therapeutic category was primarily due to a decline in sales of our CLENZIderm product line.&#160;&#160;Licensing fees remained fairly flat at $4.4&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our aggregate sales growth was composed of $0.3&#160;million in the U.S., and a $1.0&#160;million increase from our International markets.&#160;&#160;The increase in International sales was primarily due to increases in the Vitamin C and Other product categories and was principally a result of: (i) a $0.7&#160;million increase in the Far East region; (ii) a $0.1 million increase from the Europe and Other Regions; (iii) a $0.1 million increase in the Middle East; and (iv) a $0.1&#160;million increase from the Americas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As previously discussed, as a result of the actions brought by the Texas state regulatory bodies in April 2011, we have ceased selling any HQ Products into the state of Texas.&#160;&#160;Despite the growth we have experienced during 2010 and 2011, we believe that until we can resume shipping HQ Products into Texas and see continued stabilization in the global economy, our future net sales could be negatively impacted.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gross margin percentage.</font>&#160;&#160;Our gross margin percentage remained fairly flat at 78.9% during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The gross margin for our physician-dispensed segment slightly declined to 78.1% as compared to 78.3% for last year.&#160;&#160;The decline in our physician-dispensed segment was primarily a result of an increase in our inventory reserve for expired product and for inventory returned related to the Texas regulatory matter, partially offset by a change in sales mix among products, favoring our higher-margin products during the year ended December 31, 2011 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our gross margin for our licensing segment increased slightly to 99.7% compared to 96.9% for last year.&#160;&#160;The increase in our licensing segment gross margin is due to a decline in license amortization expense and royalties expense related to products containing a specific Kinetin concentration, during the year ended December 31, 2011 (see &#8220;Impairment of License&#8221; discussion under &#8220;Overview&#8221;), as compared to the prior year.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales also includes outbound shipping and handling, work order <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">scrap, licensing and royalty fees related to licensed intellectual property, depreciation and amortization attributable to products sold, and an inventory reserve for shrinkage and write-downs.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Selling, general and administrative.</font>&#160;&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of salaries and other personnel-related costs, professional fees, insurance costs, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization not attributable to products sold, warehousing costs, marketing costs, travel expenses, general and administrative support expenses and other selling expenses.&#160;&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $2.5&#160;million to $71.9&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $69.4&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The increase was primarily due to the following: (i) a $1.9 million increase in costs associated with the litigation and settlement of matters related to Dr. Obagi (see Notes 9 and 10 to our Consolidated Financial Statements); (ii) a $1.4 million increase in professional fees primarily related to consultants for our operations group and towards the evaluation of strategic alternatives to grow the business; (iii) $1.0 million in expenses related to the Texas regulatory matter, which includes costs for coordinating the return of product from our customers residing in Texas, as well as legal and other related costs; (iv) a $0.9 million increase in other marketing principally due to increased efforts in market research and consumer engagement initiatives; (v) a $0.6 million increase in promotions and training expenses; (vi) $0.5 million in impairment charges (see Note 2 to our Consolidated Financial Statements);&#160;&#160;(vii) a $0.1 million increase in non-cash compensation; and (viii) a $0.1 million increase in other expenses.&#160;&#160;These increases were partially offset by: (i) a $1.7 million decrease in headcount-related expenses primarily due to a decrease in commissions and bonus; (ii) a $1.3 million decrease in bad debt expense, due to the provision on a non-performing international distributor of $0.5 million during the year ended December 31, 2010, and due to an improvement in collections, reducing the number of accounts written-off; (iii) a $0.8 million decrease in expenses related to the secondary offering completed in November 2010; (iv) a $0.1 million decrease in rent expense due to the termination of the Agreement with Dr. Obagi in September 2010; and (v) a $0.1 million decrease in depreciation and amortization. &#160;As a percentage of net sales, selling, general and administrative expenses in the year ended December 31, 2011 increased to 63% as compared to 62% for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;We anticipate operating costs to increase, due to&#160;our investment in certain strategic initiatives during fiscal year 2012.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Research and development.</font>&#160;&#160;Research and development expenses decreased $1.7&#160;million to $2.2&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $3.9&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The decrease was primarily due to: (i) a $1.1 million decrease in expenses related to the development of line extensions and reformulations of existing products; (ii) a $0.5 million decrease in accelerated advisory and related fees pursuant to the termination of the Agreement with Dr. Obagi in September 2010; and (iii) a $0.1 million decrease in expenses related to the development of new products.&#160;&#160;The decline in our research and development costs is primarily due to the timing of our research and development activities and we have not reduced, nor do we intend to reduce, our long-term emphasis on research and development.&#160;&#160;As a percentage of net sales, research and development costs in the year ended December 31, 2011 were 2% as compared to 3% in the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest income and Interest expense.</font>&#160;&#160;Interest income declined to $35,000 for the year ended December 31, 2011 from $89,000 for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;We earn interest income from the investment of our cash balance into higher interest-yielding certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;The decline is due to a decline in our average cash and cash equivalents, including short-term investments, from $36.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2010 to $24.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2011, and a decline in our weighted average interest rate from 0.30% during the year ended December 31, 2010 to 0.24% during the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Interest expense increased to $143,000 during the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $71,000 for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Interest expense primarily consists of amortization of debt issuance costs and commitment fees related to our Credit and Term Loan Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Income taxes.</font>&#160;&#160;Income tax expense decreased $0.4&#160;million to $5.9&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2011, as compared to $6.3&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our effective tax rate was 37.0% for the year ended December 31, 2011 and 40.1% for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The difference is primarily due to the impact of the 2011 research and development credit and a decrease in our state tax expense as a result of the adoption for California purposes of single sales factor apportionment.&#160;&#160;In addition certain costs incurred during the secondary offering and stock repurchase completed in November 2010 were not deductible for tax purposes during the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net sales increased by $8.7&#160;million to $112.8&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to $104.1&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Overall, we believe our growth during the year ended December 31, 2010 is primarily due to a larger base of active accounts, higher level of patient visits due to increased consumer confidence versus last year, the launch of new products and the average price increase of 4% on our products implemented on January 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Physician-dispensed sales increased $8.9 million to $108.4 million during the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to $99.5 million during the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;We experienced an increase in the majority of our product categories as follows: (i) an increase in Vitamin C of $4.0 million, of which $1.7 million was attributable to our normal to oily line extension of Obagi-C Rx launched in January 2010; (ii) an increase in Nu-Derm sales of $3.1&#160;million; (iii) a $2.1&#160;million increase in Elasticity sales, of which $1.1 million was attributable to the launch of our ELASTILash product in October 2010; and (iv) an increase in the Other category of $1.1 million.&#160;&#160;The growth in the Other category was primarily attributable to the launch of Refissa in September 2009, which accounted for $0.7 million of the increase.&#160;&#160;These increases were partially offset by a decrease of $1.4 million in the Therapeutic category.&#160;&#160;The decline in the Therapeutic category was primarily attributable to the increased promotional activity surrounding the launch of our Rosaclear product in January 2009 and our exit of the pharmacy channel in April 2009.&#160;&#160;Licensing fees decreased by $0.2&#160;million due to a decline in unit sales by our Japanese partner Rohto during the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our aggregate sales growth was composed of $9.1&#160;million in the U.S., partially offset by a $0.2&#160;million decrease from our International markets and a decline in licensing fees of $0.2 million.&#160;&#160;The decline in International sales was primarily due to declines in the Therapeutic and Other product categories and was principally a result of a $0.8&#160;million decrease in the Far East region; partially offset by: (i) a $0.4 million increase in the Middle East; (ii) a $0.1&#160;million increase from the Americas; and (iii) a $0.1&#160;million increase from the Europe and Other regions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gross margin percentage.</font>&#160;&#160;Our gross margin percentage increased slightly to 79.0% for the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to 78.8% for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The overall increase is primarily attributable to an increase in gross margin for our physician-dispensed segment, which increased to 78.3% compared to 78.0% for the same period last year.&#160;&#160;The improvement was primarily a result of: (i) an increase in sales volumes primarily in our Nu-Derm and Vitamin C product categories; (ii) an average price increase of 4% on our products implemented on January 1, 2010; and a (iii) a decrease in sales volumes in our Therapeutic products, which have a lower margin than most of our other product categories; partially offset by a $0.7 million increase in product costs, largely in our Other product category.&#160;&#160;Our gross margin for our licensing segment increased slightly to 96.9% compared to 96.8% for the same period last year.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Selling, general and administrative.</font>&#160;&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $10.2&#160;million to $69.4&#160;million during the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to $59.2&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The increase was primarily due to the following: (i) $6.0 million in expenses for matters related to Dr. Obagi, including expenses related to pending litigation of approximately $5.6 million and $0.4 million related to the termination of the agreement dated as of June 29, 2006 (&#8220;2006 Agreement&#8221;), in September 2010, which includes the write-off of prepaid rent and leasehold improvements at a Beverly Hills location leased by us; (ii) a $2.3 million increase in salaries and related expenses due to an increase in sales commissions, accrued bonus and an increase in marketing and sales force headcount; (iii) $1.0 million in severance and other related charges in connection with the departure of Steven R. </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Research and development.</font>&#160;&#160;Research and development expenses decreased $0.5&#160;million to $3.9&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to $4.4&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;During 2010 we recorded $0.5 million in accelerated advisory and related fees pursuant to the termination of the 2006 Agreement with Dr. Obagi.&#160;&#160;In addition, salaries and related expenses increased $0.3 million.&#160;&#160;These increases were offset by: (i) a $0.6 million decrease in expenses related to the development of line extensions and reformulations of existing products; (ii) a $0.5 million decrease in expenses related to the development of new products; and (iii) $0.2 million in grant funds received under the Qualifying Therapeutic Discovery Grant Program administered by the Internal Revenue Service and the Department of Health and Human Services in support of the Company&#8217;s development of Nu-Derm for the treatment of melasma, which were recorded as an offset to research and development expense.&#160;&#160;As a percentage of net sales, research and development costs in the year ended December 31, 2010 were 3% as compared to 4% in the year ended December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Income taxes.</font>&#160;&#160;Income tax expense decreased $0.8&#160;million to $6.3&#160;million for year ended December 31, 2010, as compared to $7.1&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Although our effective tax rate increased 1.4% to 40.1% for the year ended December 31, 2010, compared to 38.7% for the year ended December 31, 2009, the decline in expense is due to a decline in income before provision for income taxes of $2.6 million.&#160;&#160;As in the&#160;prior year, the effective tax rate includes the tax benefit derived from the research and development credit during the year ended December 31, 2010. The increase in the effective tax rate is primarily due to certain costs incurred during the secondary offering and stock repurchase completed in November 2010 not being deductible for tax purposes during the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are operating in an uncertain and volatile economic environment, which could have unanticipated adverse effects on our business.&#160;&#160;The pharmaceutical industry has been impacted by the volatility in the financial markets, including declines in stock prices, and by uncertain economic conditions.&#160;&#160;Increases in food and fuel prices, changes in the availability of consumer credit and housing markets, actual and potential job losses among many sectors of the economy, significant declines in the stock market resulting in large losses to consumer retirement and investment accounts, and uncertainty regarding future federal tax and economic policies have all added to declines in consumer confidence and curtailed consumer spending.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The recent recession and ongoing tightening of credit in financial markets has, in some cases, adversely impacted our customers&#8217; cash flow and ability to access sufficient credit in a timely manner, which, in turn, has impacted their ability to make timely payments to us.&#160;&#160;In light of these circumstances, and in order to remain competitive in the marketplace, for certain selected customers who we deemed to be creditworthy based upon their prior payment history, we extended our standard payment terms from net 30 days to net 60 days for selected product purchases made in connection with certain sales promotion programs.&#160;&#160;Such extension does not represent a permanent change to the payment terms for such customers but, rather, was applicable only to specified purchases made by such customers in connection with the applicable sales promotion program.&#160;&#160;Sales of products having net 60 day payment terms represented 53% of our net sales for the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160; Although we have extended our credit terms for certain purchases made by certain qualified customers, we have seen improvement in our DSO from 66 days as of December 31, 2010 to 60 days as of December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">It is unclear how long the current economic environment will continue, whether there will be new events that could contribute to additional deterioration, and if so, what effect such events could have on our business in 2012.&#160;&#160;As <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">noted above, to facilitate more rapid growth, we plan to invest in a new e-Commerce platform and fulfillment center and, as the opportunities arise, the commercialization of new application of our current products, the continuing development of our pipeline of products and the in licensing or acquisition of new product opportunities.&#160;&#160;While we plan to increase our investments in these initiatives, we expect to continue to generate positive cash flow through our operations.</font> </font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had no outstanding balance on the Facility or Term Loans.&#160;&#160;We were in compliance with all financial and non-financial covenants under the Credit and Term Loan Agreement as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;We expect to be in compliance with both our non-financial and financial covenants during 2012; however, economic conditions or the occurrence of any of the significant events discussed above under &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; could cause noncompliance with our financial covenants.<a name="eolPage48"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expect to be able to manage our working capital levels and capital expenditure amounts to maintain sufficient levels of liquidity.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, we had approximately $52.2&#160;million and $36.0&#160;million, respectively, in working capital.&#160;&#160;We invested approximately $0.5 million in capital expenditures during the year ended December 31, 2011, which largely consisted of software and IT upgrades.&#160;&#160;In 2012, we expect to spend approximately $2.9 million in capital expenditures, primarily related to an e-Commerce platform and fulfillment center, and software and IT upgrades.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash requirements for our business</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Historically, we have generated cash from operations in excess of working capital requirements and through private and public sales of common stock.&#160;&#160;We currently invest our cash and cash equivalents in large money market funds.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, we had approximately $35.0&#160;million and $15.1 million, respectively, of cash and cash equivalents.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 9, 2011, we entered into an amendment (the &#8220;Amendment&#8221;) to the Credit and Term Loan Agreement, dated as of November 3, 2010 (the &#8220;Original Agreement&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of the Original Agreement, we have access to: (i) up to $20.0 million in a revolving credit facility; and (ii) one or more term loans in an aggregate amount of up to $15.0 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the terms of the Original Agreement, we were entitled to borrow under the Term Loans until the earliest to occur of: (i) the date the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the Term Loans equaled $15.0 million; (ii) May 3, 2011; or (iii) the date we requested to close out the Term Loans.&#160;&#160;The Amendment, among other things, extends the eligible draw period of the Term Loans for a year, so that we may now borrow under them until the earliest to occur of: (i) the date the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the Term Loans equals $15.0 million; (ii) May 3, 2012; or (iii) the date we request to close out the Term Loans.&#160;&#160;The Facility will terminate, and any amounts outstanding under the Facility will be due on July 1, 2012 and all amounts outstanding under the Term Loans will be due five years after the last day we request to close out the Term Loans, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of the Credit and Term Loan Agreement.&#160;&#160;As of the date of the Amendment, we had no outstanding balance on the Facility or the Term Loans.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Any borrowings under the Credit and Term Loan Agreement will bear variable interest based on a margin, at our option, over prime rate or LIBOR as defined in the Credit and Term Loan Agreement.&#160;&#160;All amounts borrowed under the Credit and Term Loan Agreement are secured by a first priority security interest in all of our tangible and intangible assets.&#160;&#160;The Credit and Term Loan Agreement contains certain financial and non-financial covenants.&#160;&#160;Non-financial covenants include, among other things, monthly and quarterly reporting of a listing of our intellectual property.&#160;&#160;Financial covenants include requirements for maintaining: (i) a minimum quick ratio; (ii) a maximum ratio of total liabilities to tangible effective net worth; and (iii) a minimum adjusted EBITDA amount; as well as limitations on (a) annual capital expenditures, (b) asset- or equity-based investments, (c) stock repurchases, which may not exceed $50.3 million, (d) dividend distributions, which may not exceed 25% of net income for the preceding fiscal year, and (e) joint venture investments, which may not exceed $2.0 million.&#160;&#160;See below for covenant compliance:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 26, 2010, we announced that our Board of Directors authorized us to repurchase up to $45.0 million of our common stock, depending on market conditions and other factors.&#160;&#160;Share repurchases could include the repurchase of shares from the selling stockholders in connection with the secondary offering completed in November 2010, as well as repurchases made through open market or privately negotiated transactions in compliance with SEC Rule 10b-18, subject to market conditions, applicable legal requirements and other factors.&#160;&#160;During the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2010, we repurchased 3,556,910 shares of our outstanding common stock for a cost of $35.0 million.&#160;&#160;No repurchases were effected during the year ended December 31, 2011, leaving us with $10.0 million available for repurchases under the program.&#160;&#160;On March 6, 2012, our Board authorized a $20.0 million increase to our stock repurchase program, resulting in the availability to repurchase up to $30.0 million of our common stock as of such date.&#160;&#160;This authorization does not obligate us to acquire any particular amount of common stock nor does it ensure that any shares will be repurchased, and it may be suspended at any time at our discretion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We continually evaluate new opportunities for products or therapeutic systems and, if and when appropriate, intend to pursue such opportunities through the acquisitions of companies, products or technologies and our own development activities.&#160;&#160;Our ability to execute on such opportunities in some circumstances may be dependent, in part, upon our ability to raise additional capital on commercially reasonable terms.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that funds from these sources will be available when needed or on terms favorable to us or our stockholders.&#160;&#160;If additional funds are raised by issuing equity securities, the percentage ownership of our stockholders will be reduced, stockholders<a name="eolPage49"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a> may experience additional dilution or such equity securities may provide for rights, preferences or privileges senior to those of the holders of our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Inflation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although at reduced levels in recent years, inflation continues to apply upward pressure on the cost of goods and services that we use.&#160;&#160;The competitive environments in many markets substantially limit our ability to fully recover these higher costs through increased selling prices.&#160;&#160;We continually seek to mitigate the adverse effects of inflation through cost containment and improved productivity and manufacturing processes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Foreign Currency Fluctuations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Approximately 4% of our net sales in 2011 were derived from operations outside the United States and were denominated in Japanese Yen.&#160;&#160;None of our international cost structure is denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.&#160;&#160;As a result, we are subject to fluctuations in sales and earnings reported in U.S. dollars due to changing currency exchange rates.&#160;&#160;We do not believe, however, that we currently have significant direct foreign currency exchange rate risk and have not hedged exposures denominated in foreign currencies.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash Flow</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Year ended December 31, 2011.</font>&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2011, net cash provided by operating activities was $19.4&#160;million.&#160;&#160;The primary sources of cash were $10.0&#160;million in net income, including the effect of: (i)&#160;adjusting for non-cash items; (ii) an increase in accounts payable and accrued liabilities through timing of payments for operational, promotional and inventory purchases; (iii) a decrease in accounts receivable through improvement in our DSO from 72 days to&#160;65 days; (iv) a decrease in income taxes receivable; and (v)&#160;a decrease in inventory through an increase in our inventory turn ratio from 4.2 to 5.2.</font></div>

<div align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net cash used in investing activities was $0.8&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;This was due to costs associated with software and IT upgrades and investments in licenses and patent-related intellectual property during the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;We anticipate spending approximately $2.9&#160;million for total capital expenditures in 2012 primarily for planned investments in an e-Commerce platform and fulfillment center, and software and IT upgrades.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cobrek Pharmaceuticals, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From November 2010 through March 2011, we entered into consulting arrangements with certain individuals affiliated with Cobrek Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (&#8220;Cobrek&#8221;) to provide consulting services to us.&#160;&#160;These individuals include: (i) Cobrek&#8217;s Vice President of Regulatory Affairs and Quality Assurance; (ii) the Chairman of the board of directors of Cobrek; (iii) a member of the board of directors of Cobrek; and (iv) a senior consultant to Cobrek.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2011, we recorded $0.9 million in aggregate fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by these four consultants.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2010, we recorded $36,000 in fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by one of the consultants, which were recorded as a component of &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses.&#8221;&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, amounts due to the four consultants aggregated $0.1 million and $36,000, respectively, and are included in &#8220;Amounts due to related parties&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We may enter into an additional consulting arrangement with Cobrek itself and may engage other employees or consultants of Cobrek to provide information and/or other services to us.&#160;&#160;In addition to the four consultants mentioned above, Albert F. Hummel, our President and Chief Executive Officer and member of our Board of Directors, is also the Chief Executive Officer, a member of the board of directors and a holder of more than 10% of the outstanding stock of Cobrek.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2011 and 2010, we recorded $0.2 million and $0.1 million, respectively, in fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by Mr. Hummel prior to entering into an employment arrangement and subsequent employment agreement with him.&#160;&#160;These expenses were recorded as a component of &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses.&#8221;&#160;&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the $0.1 million in fees due to Mr. Hummel, were included in &#8220;Amounts due to related parties&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;See Note 10, &#8220;Albert F. Hummel Employment Agreement&#8221; in our Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for further information.</font></div>

<div align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 15, 2010, we entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement with the selling stockholders, under which we were obligated to purchase from the selling stockholders $35.0 million worth of our common stock, subject to certain conditions.&#160;&#160;The purchase price per share to be paid to the selling stockholders was to be the same price paid by the underwriter to purchase shares from the selling stockholders in the secondary offering completed in November 2010.&#160;&#160;However, if the purchase price to be paid was greater than $13.00, we would not purchase any shares from the selling stockholders.&#160;&#160;In addition, the purchase of the shares by us was conditioned on the sale of shares in the secondary offering.</font></div>

(&#8220;the Marketer&#8221;) (collectively, the &#8220;Dr. Obagi Parties&#8221;), effective as of October 4, 2010.&#160;&#160;In connection with the termination of the 2006 Agreement, we accelerated the payment of $0.5 million in certain fees and expenses (included within &#8220;Research and development expenses&#8221;) during the third quarter 2010, that otherwise would have been paid during the remainder of the original term, which was for five years and would have otherwise ended on June 29, 2011.&#160;&#160;No additional amounts were paid to the Dr. Obagi Parties as a result of the termination.&#160;&#160;In addition, as a result of the termination, we determined that our leasehold improvements in connection with a lease with the Marketer was impaired, resulting in the write-off of $0.3 million in leasehold improvements at the Beverly Hills property and $0.2 million in prepaid rent (included within &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">New Accounting Standards</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2011, the FASB issued authoritative guidance in ASC 220, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Comprehensive Income</font>, on the presentation of other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;The new guidance eliminates the option to present components of other comprehensive income as part of the statement of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity and requires an entity to present either one continuous statement of net income and other comprehensive income or two separate, but consecutive, statements.&#160;&#160;Further, the guidance requires reclassification adjustments from other comprehensive income to net income to be presented on the face of the financial statements.&#160;&#160;However, in December 2011, the FASB issued follow-up guidance to defer the requirement to present reclassification adjustments from other comprehensive income on the face of the financial statements and allow entities to continue to report reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;While the new guidance changes the presentation of comprehensive income, there are no changes to the components that are recognized in net income or other comprehensive income under current accounting guidance.&#160;&#160;We will adopt this new guidance beginning the first quarter of the fiscal year ending December 31, 2012, and will apply it retrospectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2011, the FASB issued authoritative guidance in ASC 350, with respect to the annual goodwill impairment test that adds a qualitative assessment allowing companies to determine whether they need to perform the two-step impairment test.&#160;&#160;The objective of the guidance is to simplify how companies test goodwill for impairment, and more specifically to reduce the cost and complexity of performing the goodwill impairment test.&#160;&#160;The guidance may change how the goodwill impairment test is performed, but should not change the timing or the measurement of goodwill impairments.&#160;&#160;We elected to adopt this accounting guidance early at the beginning of our third quarter of 2011 on a prospective basis for goodwill impairment tests.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this standard did not have an impact on our consolidated financial statements and footnote disclosures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="eolPage51"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a><a name="item7aquantitative"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>ITEM 7A:&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We invest our excess cash primarily in large money market funds and certificates of deposit with maturity dates no greater than one year.&#160;&#160;We do not utilize derivative financial instruments, derivative commodity instruments or other market risk sensitive instruments, positions or transactions in any material fashion.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we believe that we are not subject to any material risks arising from changes in interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices, equity prices or other market changes that affect market risk sensitive instruments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although substantially all of our sales and purchases are denominated in U.S. dollars, future fluctuations in the value of the U.S. dollar may affect the price competitiveness of our products outside the U.S.&#160;&#160;We do not believe, however, that we currently have significant direct foreign currency exchange rate risk and have not hedged exposures denominated in foreign currencies.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Rate Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our interest income and expense is more sensitive to fluctuations in the general level of U.S. prime rate and LIBOR interest rates than to changes in rates in other markets.&#160;&#160;Changes in U.S. LIBOR interest rates affect the interest earned on our cash and cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, we had approximately $35.0&#160;million of cash and cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;If the interest rates on our cash and cash equivalents were to increase or decrease by 1% for the year, annual interest income would increase or decrease by approximately $0.4&#160;million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Risks</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The recent recession has had an adverse impact on the financial services industry, including insurance companies, some of whom provide insurance coverage to us.&#160;&#160;To the extent we have any claims in the future and such insurance providers are unable, due to their financial condition, to pay covered claims, we could experience adverse <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">impacts on our cash flow and cash reserves.&#160;&#160;We have no way of knowing whether or not any insurance providers that are financially stable at this time will experience financial difficulties in the future that could impact their ability to pay covered claims.</font> </font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<a name="eolPage52"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>&#160;</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="item8finstatements"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>ITEM 8:&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of the end of the period covered by this Report, we carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&#160;13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Exchange Act).&#160;&#160;Based upon that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective in providing reasonable assurance that information is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules, regulations and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules&#160;13a-15(f) and 15(d)-15(f) of the Exchange Act).&#160;&#160;Under the supervision and with the participation of management, including our Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based upon the framework in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework</font> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160;&#160;Based on that evaluation, our management concluded that Obagi&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2011 has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers&#160;LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in its Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm under Part&#160;IV, Item&#160;15 of this Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There has been no change in our internal control over financial reporting during the most recent fiscal quarter that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="item9botherinfo"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>ITEM 9B:&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;OTHER INFORMATION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Obagi</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Resolution of Texas Matter</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">By letter dated February 29, 2012 the Agency notified the AG that it would be closing its pending investigation and enforcement action against us relating to our promotion, sales and distribution of HQ Products in Texas effective that date and withdrew its April 13, 2011 referral of the matter to the AG.&#160;&#160;The Agency based its decision on:&#160;&#160;(i) a directive that the Agency set priorities for enforcement and allocate its resources and concentrate its efforts on cases that represent the greatest risk to public health and safety; (ii) a FDA Q&amp;A document issued in 2010 wherein the FDA acknowledged the potential medical benefits of hydroquinone-containing products for a certain medical condition, the uncertainty of the public health risks associated with the ingredient and its intent to conduct long term studies through the NTP; and (iii) its acknowledgment of the relevance of the FDA&#8217;s CPG policy statement that FDA has been using to guide its staff and industry concerning the FDA&#8217;s enforcement priorities for unapproved drug products.&#160;&#160;The Agency also noted that it did not have sufficient evidence to conclude that there is an immediate risk to public health and safety from the topical use of products containing hydroquinone.&#160;&#160;No monetary penalties or other administrative fees were levied against us as the result of the Agency&#8217;s investigation and no lawsuit was ever filed by the AG against us.&#160;&#160;Beginning in April 2011 we voluntarily ceased selling any products containing 4% hydroquinone into the state of Texas.&#160;&#160;In addition, we implemented a plan that enabled our customers in Texas to return any of these products (that had not otherwise been </font></div>

<div align="left"><br>
</div>

<div align="left">
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
