<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, diluted earnings per share do not include the impact of common stock options and restricted stock units then outstanding of 1,043,392, 451,000 and 1,491,396, respectively, as the effect of their inclusion would be anti-dilutive.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">New Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2011, the FASB issued authoritative guidance in ASC 220, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Comprehensive Income</font>, on the presentation of other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;The new guidance eliminates the option to present components of other comprehensive income as part of the statement of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity and requires an entity to present either one continuous statement of net income and other comprehensive income or two separate, but consecutive, statements.&#160;&#160;Further, the guidance requires reclassification adjustments from other comprehensive income to net income to be presented on the face of the financial statements.&#160;&#160;However, in December 2011, the FASB issued follow-up guidance to defer the requirement to present reclassification adjustments from other comprehensive income on the face of the financial statements and allow entities to continue to report reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;While the new guidance changes the presentation of comprehensive income, there are no changes to the components that are recognized in net income or other comprehensive income under current accounting guidance.&#160;&#160;The Company will adopt this new guidance beginning the first quarter of the fiscal year ending December 31, 2012, and will apply it retrospectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2011, the FASB issued authoritative guidance in ASC 350, with respect to the annual goodwill impairment test that adds a qualitative assessment allowing companies to determine whether they need to perform the two-step impairment test.&#160;&#160;The objective of the guidance is to simplify how companies test goodwill for impairment, and more specifically to reduce the cost and complexity of performing the goodwill impairment test.&#160;&#160;The guidance may change how the goodwill impairment test is performed, but should not change the timing or the measurement of goodwill impairments.&#160;&#160;The Company elected to adopt this accounting guidance early at the beginning of its third quarter of 2011 on a prospective basis for goodwill impairment tests.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this standard did not have an impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and footnote disclosures.<a name="FIS_UNIDENTIFIED_TABLE_22"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>&#160;&#160;See Note 2 &#8211; <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font> &#8211; <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Intangible Assets</font>, for further discussion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;3: Composition of Certain Financial Statement Captions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Obagi Medical Products, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Dollars in thousands, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>

</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;4: Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loans and Capital Lease Obligations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 9, 2011, the Company entered into an amendment (the &#8220;Amendment&#8221;) to the Amended and Restated Revolving Credit and Term Loan Agreement, dated as of November 3, 2010, among the Company, Comerica Bank and the other financial institutions signatory thereto (the &#8220;Original Agreement&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of the Original Agreement, the Company has access to: (i) up to $20,000 in a revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Facility&#8221;); and (ii) one or more term loans in an aggregate amount of up to $15,000 (the &#8220;Term Loans&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the terms of the Original Agreement, the Company was entitled to borrow under the Term Loans until the earliest to occur of: (i) the date the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the Term Loans equaled $15,000; (ii) May 3, 2011; or (iii) the date the Company requested to close out the Term Loans.&#160;&#160;The Amendment, effective May 4, 2011, among other things, extends the eligible draw period of the Term Loans for a year, so that the Company may now borrow under them until the earliest to occur of: (i) the date the aggregate outstanding principal balance of the Term Loans equals $15,000; (ii) May 3, 2012; or (iii) the date the Company requests to close out the Term Loans.&#160;&#160;As of the date of the Amendment, the Company had no outstanding balance on the Facility or the Term Loans.&#160;&#160;The Facility will terminate, and any amounts outstanding under the Facility will be due on July 1, 2012 and all amounts outstanding under the Terms Loans will be due five years after the last day of the Term Loan Draw Period, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of the Credit and Term Loan Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Any borrowings under the Facility and Term Loans will bear variable interest based on a margin, at the Company&#8217;s option, over prime rate or LIBOR as defined in the Credit and Term Loan Agreement.&#160;&#160;All amounts borrowed under the Credit and Term Loan Agreement are secured by a first priority security interest in all of the Company&#8217;s tangible and intangible assets.&#160;&#160;Commencing January 2011, the Company must pay a revolving credit facility fee annually in arrears of $55.&#160;&#160;The Credit and Term Loan Agreement contains certain financial and non-financial covenants.&#160;&#160;Non-financial covenants include, among other things, monthly and quarterly reporting of a listing of the Company&#8217;s intellectual property.&#160;&#160;Financial covenants include requirements for maintaining: (i) a minimum quick ratio; (ii) a maximum ratio of total liabilities to net worth; and (iii) a minimum adjusted EBITDA amount; as well as limitations on (a) annual capital expenditures, (b) asset- or equity-based investments, (c) stock repurchases, which may not exceed $50,300, (d) dividend distributions, which may not exceed 25% of net income for the preceding fiscal year, and (e) joint venture investments, which may not exceed $2,000.&#160;&#160;In March 2012, the Company received a commitment from Comerica Bank to amend certain terms of the Credit and Term Loan Agreement.&#160;&#160;See Note 15 for further information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, the Company did not have an outstanding balance on its Facility or Term Loans.&#160;&#160;If the Company had a balance on its Facility or Term Loans as of December 31, 2011, the applicable variable prime rate and LIBOR rates, as defined in the Credit and Term Loan Agreement, would have been 3.25% and 2.13%, respectively.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, the Company was in compliance with all financial and non-financial covenants under the Credit and Term Loan Agreement. &#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;5: Common Stock</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock Repurchases</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 26, 2010, the Company announced that its Board of Directors has authorized the Company to repurchase up to $45,000 of its common stock, depending on market conditions and other factors.&#160;&#160;Share repurchases have included the repurchase of shares from the selling stockholders following completion of the secondary offering completed in November 2010 (see Note 1), and may include future repurchases made through open market or privately negotiated transactions in compliance with SEC Rule 10b-18, subject to market conditions, applicable legal requirements and other factors.&#160;&#160;This authorization does not obligate the Company to acquire any particular amount of common stock nor does it ensure that any shares will be repurchased, and it may be suspended at any time at the Company&#8217;s discretion.&#160;&#160;On March 6, 2012 the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors increased the amount available to the Company to repurchase its common stock.&#160;&#160;See Note 15 for further information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the year ended December 31, 2010, the Company repurchased 3,556,910 shares from the selling stockholders pursuant to a Stock Purchase Agreement for $35,000 at a price of $9.84 per share, which was equal to the public offering price of shares sold by the selling stockholders in the secondary offering in November 2010 of $10.25 per share less the applicable underwriter&#8217;s discount.&#160;&#160;This amount is reflected in &#8220;Treasury stock&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;See Note 9 for further discussion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stockholder Rights Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In December 2011 the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors adopted a stockholder rights plan pursuant to which it declared a dividend of one preferred share purchase right for each outstanding share of its common stock, payable to stockholders of record on January 10, 2012.&#160;&#160;The rights become exercisable upon the earlier of ten days after a person or group of affiliated or associated persons has acquired 20% or more of the outstanding shares of its common stock or ten business days after a tender offer or exchange offer has commenced that would result in a person or group of affiliated or associated persons beneficially owning 20% or more of its outstanding common stock.&#160;&#160;The stockholder rights plan expires upon the earliest of: (i) December 23, 2014, three years from the date of its adoption; (ii) December 23, 2012, if not submitted to stockholders for ratification; and (iii) June 6, 2012, the date of the annual meeting if&#160;the Company's&#160;stockholders vote against its ratification.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, there were no stockholders who owned 20% or more of the Company&#8217;s outstanding shares of common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;7: Concentrations of Credit Risk and Significant Customers</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, no single customer accounted for 10% or more of the Company&#8217;s net sales.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company currently has no internal manufacturing capabilities and outsources all of its product manufacturing.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Company does not have long-term contracts with most of these third-party manufacturers.&#160;&#160;Although there are a limited number of third-party manufacturers, management believes that other suppliers could provide similar services on comparable terms.&#160;&#160;A change in suppliers, however, could cause a delay in manufacturing and a possible loss of sales, which would affect operating results adversely.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company currently has limited internal research and development capabilities and primarily outsources its product research and development to third-party research labs.&#160;&#160;Although there are a limited number of third-party research labs, management believes that other labs could provide similar services on comparable terms.&#160;&#160;A change in providers, however, could cause a delay in the Company&#8217;s ability to develop and deliver products on a timely and competitive basis, which could adversely affect operating results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;8: Royalty Licensee Agreements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the patent license agreement dated June&#160;26, 2003 with a third party, the Company licensed four interlocking method and formulation patents in exchange for non-refundable license fees for the first three years of the agreement.&#160;&#160;The agreement also calls for the Company to pay royalties on net sales of products covered by the licensed patents.&#160;&#160;Such royalties are to be paid on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, related royalties of $363, $404 and $339, respectively, have been included as a component of &#8220;Cost of sales.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The initial term of this agreement was three years but is renewable annually at the option of the Company, provided that the Company pays an annual non-refundable renewal license fee to the licensor.&#160;&#160;The patent license agreement may terminate at the licensor&#8217;s option upon a merger or acquisition of the Company that is not approved by the licensor, whose approval may not be unreasonably withheld, and may be cancelled by either party upon default.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company also competes in the Japanese retail skin care markets through a strategic licensing agreement with Rohto Pharmaceutical&#160;Co.,&#160;Ltd. (&#8220;Rohto&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Rohto is a Japanese pharmaceutical manufacturer and distributor.&#160;&#160;Under the agreement, Rohto is licensed to manufacture and sell a series of OTC products developed by it under the Obagi brand name, as well as Obagi-C (a Vitamin C based topical serum in various concentrations), in the Japanese drug store channel and the Company receives a royalty based upon sales of Obagi branded products in Japan by Rohto.&#160;&#160;The Company also had other licensing arrangements in Japan to market and sell OTC product systems under the Obagi brand, both for in-office use in facial procedures, as well as for sale as a take-home product kit in the spa channel, which it chose not to renew in January 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 4, 2008, the Company entered into an amendment to the original agreement with Rohto.&#160;&#160;The amendment extends the term of agreement to December 4, 2017 and&#160;amends the Territory (as defined in the Rohto agreement) to areas outside Japan, subject to separate written agreement(s) to be developed.&#160;&#160;The Channel (as defined in the Rohto agreement) has been expanded to include department stores, including mail-order and internet activities to support such expansion, provided that the parties complete a joint development plan.&#160;&#160;The parties have also agreed to work together to up-brand the Obagi products sold in the various channels and work cooperatively on messaging, branding and product imaging.&#160;&#160;Under the amendment, the Company has also agreed to provide an exclusive royalty bearing license to sell and/or manufacture certain products developed by the Company or Rohto, or jointly developed by the Company and Rohto.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 4, 2008, the Company and Rohto entered into a License and Supply Agreement (the &#8220;Bi-mineral Agreement&#8221;) whereby the Company granted Rohto an exclusive right to manufacture, market and sell the Company&#8217;s bi-mineral collagen and elastin enhancing products in all channels (other than the aesthetic and spa channels) in Japan.&#160;&#160;Rohto also has the right to develop improvements to such products or new products related to the products.&#160;&#160;The initial term of the Bi-mineral Agreement is for five years, through December 4, 2013, with an optional five-year extension, and calls for certain annual sales volume and expense commitments on behalf of Rohto.&#160;&#160;If such commitments are not met, the Company shall have the right to terminate the agreement or render it non-exclusive.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cobrek Pharmaceuticals, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From November 2010 through March 2011, the Company entered into consulting arrangements with certain individuals affiliated with Cobrek Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (&#8220;Cobrek&#8221;) to provide consulting services to the Company.&#160;&#160;These individuals include: (i) Cobrek&#8217;s Vice President of Regulatory Affairs and Quality Assurance; (ii) the Chairman of the board of directors of Cobrek; (iii) a member of the board of directors of Cobrek; and (iv) a senior consultant to Cobrek.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2011, the Company recorded $875 in aggregate fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by the same four consultants, of which $794 and $81 were recorded as components of &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221; and &#8220;Research and development expenses, respectively.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2010, the Company recorded $36 in fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by one of the consultants, which were recorded as a component of &#8220;Research and development expenses.&#8221; As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, amounts due to the four consultants aggregated $84 and $36, respectively, and are included in &#8220;Amounts due to related parties&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company may enter into an additional consulting arrangement with Cobrek itself and may engage other employees or consultants of Cobrek to provide formulation and/or other services to the Company.&#160;&#160;In addition to the four consultants mentioned above, Albert F. Hummel, the Company&#8217;s President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors, is also the Chief Executive Officer, a member of the board of directors and a holder of more than 10% of the outstanding stock of Cobrek.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2011 and 2010, the Company recorded $160 and $111, respectively, in fees and related expenses for consulting services provided by Mr. Hummel prior to entering into an employment arrangement and subsequent employment agreement (see Note 10) with him.&#160;&#160;These expenses were recorded as a component of &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses.&#8221;&#160;&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the $111 in fees due to Mr. Hummel, were included in &#8220;Amounts due to related parties&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock Purchase Agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 15, 2010, the Company entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement with the selling stockholders, under which the Company was obligated to purchase from the selling stockholders $35,000 worth of the Company&#8217;s common stock, subject to certain conditions.&#160;&#160;The purchase price per share to be paid to the selling stockholders was to be the same price paid by the underwriter to purchase shares from the selling stockholders in the secondary offering discussed in Note 1.&#160;&#160;However, if the purchase price to be paid was greater than $13.00, the Company would not purchase any shares from the selling stockholders.&#160;&#160;In addition, the purchase of the shares by the Company was conditioned on the sale of shares in the secondary offering.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Following the completion of the secondary offering of 2,690,244 shares on November 24, 2010, the Company repurchased 3,556,910 shares from the selling stockholders at a price of $9.84 per share, which was equal to the public offering price of $10.25 per share less the applicable underwriter&#8217;s discount, on November 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;Upon completion of both transactions the selling stockholders ceased to own any shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As discussed above, as of November 30, 2010, Zein&#160;Obagi, M.D., the Company&#8217;s former executive medical director and board member, ceased to own any shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.&#160;&#160;As a result, subsequent to November 30, 2010, Dr. Obagi and his affiliates are no longer considered related parties.&#160;&#160;Dr. Obagi was granted the right to purchase products from the Company at a discount equal to the maximum discount offered to the Company&#8217;s unrelated customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As mentioned in Note 3, on September 2, 2010, the Company exercised its right to terminate the 2006 Agreement with the Dr. Obagi Parties, effective as of October 4, 2010.&#160;&#160;The 2006 Agreement provided, among other things, that the Obagi Entities and/or the Marketer would promote and provide services to support the marketing of the Company&#8217;s products, including the oversight of property the Company leased in Beverly Hills, California.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Obagi Entities would have to be available to advise and assist the Company in the formulation and clinical testing of new products and, at the Company&#8217;s request, to chair an annual symposium and up to two clinical advisory meetings per year.&#160;&#160;The 2006 Agreement also contained provisions protecting the Company&#8217;s intellectual property rights, including trademarks, and confidential information, and limiting competition by the Dr. Obagi Parties.&#160;&#160;The Company agreed to pay Obagi Inc. an annual retainer of approximately $570.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company agreed to pay Obagi Inc. an annual fee of $200 for the first two years of the 2006 Agreement for the development of Proderm products, a line of skincare products.&#160;&#160;At the end of the two years, the Company had the option to continue to sell Proderm products, in exchange for an annual royalty payment.&#160;&#160;The Company did not exercise this option.&#160;&#160; In addition, the Company agreed to pay Obagi Inc. royalty fees for developing other products identified in the agreement equal to 5% of the Company&#8217;s net revenues from sales of those products.&#160;&#160;As there were no products commercialized under the 2006 Agreement, the Company did not pay any royalties pursuant to the 2006 Agreement during the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009.&#160;&#160;The Company also agreed to pay certain fees and expenses for certain additional training and educational services and clinical studies, as well as 50% of all invoiced commercially reasonable marketing design and development (not production) expenses associated with the opening of the property in Beverly Hills, up to $100.&#160;&#160; The original term of the 2006 Agreement was five years, and would have otherwise ended on June 29, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The termination of the 2006 Agreement does not relieve the Dr. Obagi Parties from their obligations to comply with certain provisions of the 2006 Agreement, particularly as they relate to a limited trademark license to Obagi Inc. and/or the Marketer, the grant to the Company of a license to have access to and utilize accounts, customer lists and other customer information and data developed in connection with the 2006 Agreement, the protection of the Company&#8217;s intellectual property rights and other additional confidential information of the Company, nor does it affect the Company&#8217;s ownership of trademarks and other intellectual property rights.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company entered into a lease agreement for the Beverly Hills property described above and a letter agreement with the Marketer as landlord dated June 29, 2006 in connection with the 2006 Agreement.&#160;&#160;The lease has a term of five years beginning August&#160;1, 2006.&#160;&#160;The base rent under the lease is $87 per year, and could be raised at a rate of 3.5% per year thereafter.&#160;&#160; As a result of the termination, the Company determined that the leasehold improvements were impaired resulting in the write-off of $258 in leasehold improvements at the Beverly Hills property and $153 in prepaid rent (included with &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221;).&#160;&#160;During the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, the Company recorded $138 and $184 in rent expense related to the agreement, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On January 9, 2008, the Company entered into an Indemnification Agreement with the Dr. Obagi Parties and ZSO, LP (the &#8220;Indemnification Agreement&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Indemnification Agreement provided for the Company to place approximately $340 in escrow in exchange for an indemnification for any liability arising from the underlying Legacy construction contract.&#160;&#160;By the terms of the June 29, 2006 letter agreement (the &#8220;2006 Letter Agreement&#8221;) by and among the Company and the Dr. Obagi Parties, the Dr. Obagi Parties were required to reimburse the Company for any amounts the Company spent on leasehold improvements in excess of $1,817.&#160;&#160;The $340 is above the $1,817 cap on leasehold improvements that the Company was responsible for under the 2006 Letter Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 14, 2008, the Company entered into a binding settlement agreement and stipulation agreement by and between Legacy, certain of the Obagi Parties and Battaglia, Inc.&#160;&#160;In this agreement, the Company was formally released from any and all remaining obligations to Legacy.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the agreement, on July 25, 2008, the Company fulfilled its obligations under the Indemnification Agreement by paying the agreed upon $340.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the 2006 Letter Agreement, as restated in the Indemnification Agreement, the Company was released from any future claims related to, and entitled to reimbursement for, the leasehold improvements of the marketing and training center over and above $1,817.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded $335 as a receivable due from Dr. Obagi as the amount was above the cap on leasehold improvements that the Company was responsible for.&#160;&#160;As Dr. Obagi disputed the balance due to the Company, as of December 31, 2008, the Company reserved $168 of the balance.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, the Company wrote off the remaining $167 as ZO Skin Health, Inc., filed a complaint in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, against the Company (see Note 10).&#160;&#160;Payments in the amount of approximately $340 over and above the $1,817 amount of leasehold improvements that the Company was responsible were never repaid by the Dr. Obagi Parties.&#160;&#160;Despite the amounts due from Dr. Obagi relating to the excess amount of leasehold improvements paid by the Company, the Company did not record a receivable due from Dr. Obagi for these amounts as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Amounts due from Dr. Obagi as of December 31, 2010 (see table below) solely consisted of trade accounts receivable and are considered collectible.</font></div>

Obagi, M.D., Zein E. Obagi, M.D., Inc., ZO Skin Health, Inc., Skin Health Properties, Inc., the Zein and Samar Obagi Trust, and Samar Obagi (collectively, the &#8220;ZO Parties&#8221;) (the &#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;) during the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;See Note 10 for a detailed description of Settlement and related litigation and other legal matters.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Texas Regulatory Matter</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2009, the Company received a letter from the Texas Department of State Health Services (the &#8220;Agency&#8221;) regarding the Company&#8217;s shipping in Texas of products containing unapproved new drugs and, specifically, referencing certain retail businesses in Texas that were selling the Company&#8217;s products containing prescription drugs over the Internet.&#160;&#160;Prior to this time, the Agency had detained products from three of the Company&#8217;s customers that sold the Company&#8217;s products on the Internet as a result of a complaint received from a third party.&#160;&#160;In its letter, the Agency alleged that the Company was shipping unapproved new drug articles to these establishments in violation of certain Texas statutes.&#160;&#160;The Company submitted its response to the Agency in January 2010 indicating why it believed it was in compliance with the Texas statutes.&#160;&#160;In May 2010, the Agency sent a letter to the Company indicating that it did not agree with the arguments set forth in the Company&#8217;s January 2010 letter.&#160;&#160;In June 2010, the Company had an in-person meeting with officials from the Agency to further discuss its concerns.&#160;&#160;In August 2010, the Company submitted additional written information to the Agency in response to the topics discussed and additional information requested by the Agency at the June meeting.&#160;&#160;From that time until April 2011, the Agency did not have any further communications with the Company.&#160;&#160;In March 2011, the Agency, in response to what the Company then understood was a new complaint, detained the Company&#8217;s products containing 4% hydroquinone (the &#8220;HQ Products&#8221;) from one of its customers as being unapproved new drugs and further cited this customer for dispensing prescription drugs without a pharmacy license in violation of various Texas statutes.&#160;&#160;Despite repeated requests, neither the Agency nor the Texas Attorney General (&#8220;AG&#8221;) has been able to identify or provide the Company with any additional complaints.&#160;&#160;In early April 2011, the Agency detained products from several more of the Company&#8217;s customers citing similar violations.&#160;&#160;Shortly thereafter, the Company attempted to contact the Agency to ascertain what the issues were that prompted the recent actions taken by the Agency against these customers.&#160;&#160;The Agency indicated to the Company that it had referred the issues related to these latest complaints to the AG for enforcement action.&#160;&#160;At the end of April 2011, the Company met with the Agency and the AG at which time the AG stated it viewed the Company to be in violation of the Texas Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act arising from the sale in Texas of the Company&#8217;s HQ Products.&#160;&#160;In July 2011, the AG reiterated its position, as noted above, to the Company in a letter.&#160;&#160;In July 2011, the Company&#8217;s counsel met with the AG to continue discussions regarding an amicable settlement of this matter.&#160;&#160;In August 2011, the AG sent a letter following up on certain aspects of the July 2011 meeting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Beginning April 2011, the Company voluntarily ceased shipping any HQ Products into the state of Texas.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company developed a plan that enabled its customers in Texas to return any of these products (that had not otherwise been detained) in their possession in exchange for a credit or refund.&#160;&#160;In February 2012, the Company was notified that the investigation has been completed and the complaint withdrawn.&#160;&#160;See Note 15 for further information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Obagi Medical Products, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Provision for Sales Returns and Allowances</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In light of the aforementioned events, the Company recorded a sales returns and allowances provision for product to be returned from its customers residing in Texas during the three months ended March 31, 2011 of $1,927, which was recorded as a component of &#8220;Accrued liabilities&#8221; and as an offset to &#8220;Net sales&#8221; during the three months ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company recorded $282 in estimated finished goods inventory to be returned and as an offset to &#8220;Cost of sales&#8221; during the three months ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s methodology for calculating the provision considered, by customer, the previous 12 months of sales history.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company engaged a third party to assist in the efforts to manage the return of product from its customers residing in Texas.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Company&#8217;s efforts, during the second and third quarters of 2011, the Company processed credits and refunds of $1,669 for returned or detained products having an inventory value of $258.&#160;&#160;In addition, during the three months ended September 30, 2011, the Company wrote off $153 in returned finished goods inventory, which was fully reserved for as of June 30, 2011, related to the matter. As of December 31, 2011, the Company did not anticipate further sales returns and allowances related to the matter.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Albert F. Hummel Employment Agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective April 21, 2011 (the &#8220;Effective Date&#8221;), the Company and Mr. Hummel, entered into an Executive Employment Agreement for a term of three years.&#160;&#160;Under the agreement, Mr. Hummel is entitled to a base salary of $500 per year, subject to annual cost of living increases or such greater increase as may be approved by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors, and an annual bonus of up to 75% of his annual base salary based upon achievement of certain Company and individual targets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On the Effective Date, the Compensation Committee granted Mr. Hummel an option to purchase 100,000 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, with an exercise price per share of $12.55, the closing selling price per share of the Company&#8217;s common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The option will vest and become exercisable with respect to 33.33% of the underlying shares per annum upon Mr. Hummel&#8217;s completion of each year of service with the Company following the Effective Date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Additionally,&#160;&#160;on the Effective Date the Compensation Committee awarded Mr. Hummel 50,000 restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) to acquire an equal number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock with no cash payment on his part other than applicable income and employment taxes.&#160;&#160;The RSUs will vest in full upon the second anniversary of the Effective Date provided Mr. Hummel remains employed by the Company on such date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Either Mr. Hummel or the Company may terminate his employment at any time.&#160;&#160;If Mr. Hummel is terminated for cause or terminates his own employment, he will be entitled to no severance.&#160;&#160;If Mr. Hummel is terminated without cause, he will be entitled to 12 months&#8217; severance.&#160;&#160;In addition he will be entitled to continuation of all benefits made generally available to all executives (including continuation of coverage under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (&#8220;COBRA&#8221;)) for 12 months, and will have a period of 12 months to exercise any options that were vested on the date of termination.&#160;&#160;In the event Mr. Hummel&#8217;s employment terminates by reason of death or disability, he will not be entitled to severance, but his designee or spouse will have a period of 12 months to exercise any options that were vested on the date of termination.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If Mr. Hummel terminates his employment for good reason, then he will be entitled to 12 months&#8217; severance and continuation of all benefits made generally available to all executives (including continuation of COBRA) for 12 months.&#160;&#160;In addition, in the event of a change in control, all options and RSUs held by Mr. Hummel will vest in full, and all options will become exercisable immediately prior to such change in control, regardless of his continued employment status.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Steven R. Carlson Separation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective October 8, 2010 (the &#8220;Carlson Effective Date&#8221;), Steven R. Carlson, resigned as the Company&#8217;s President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of its Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;In connection with Mr. Carlson&#8217;s departure, the Company entered into a Separation Agreement and Release (&#8220;Separation Agreement&#8221;) with Mr. Carlson on October 15, 2010.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of the Separation Agreement, Mr. Carlson will receive the payments and other benefits to which he would have otherwise been entitled had his employment been terminated without cause under the Employment Agreement, dated March 1, 2005, between the Company and Mr. Carlson as amended (&#8220;Employment Agreement&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As a result, on the Carlson Effective Date, Mr. Carlson received $66, representing his unpaid base salary through that date as well as accrued vacation pay.&#160;&#160;On April 11, 2011, in accordance with the terms of the Employment Agreement, Mr. Carlson also received: (i) $750, which is equal to 18 months of his base salary, and (ii) $221 representing the pro rata portion of amounts otherwise payable to Mr. Carlson under the Company&#8217;s 2010 Performance Incentive Plan that had been accrued as of the Carlson Effective Date.&#160;&#160;The Company will also pay for premiums for continuation of his health coverage under COBRA for a period of up to 18 months.&#160;&#160;In addition, the vesting of the 90,917 shares subject to options held by Mr. Carlson as of the Carlson Effective Date (equal to the number of shares subject to those options that would have vested over the 12 month period following the Carlson Effective Date) accelerated and such options became immediately exercisable with respect to those shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although there were no provisions for repurchase of the options to purchase the Company&#8217;s common stock held by Mr. Carlson, under the Separation Agreement in November 2010, the Company agreed to make to Mr. Carlson a lump sum payment of $875 to extinguish all of his rights in all options to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock outstanding on the Carlson Effective Date, without regard to whether such options were then vested and exercisable, would have become exercisable or would have expired subsequent to the Carlson Effective Date.&#160;&#160;The calculation of such lump sum amount was determined based upon the difference between $11.26 per share (the 90-day trailing average closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock as of the Carlson Effective Date) and the exercise price in effect for each of the 541,835 vested and exercisable, in-the-money options held by Mr. Carlson on the Carlson Effective Date.&#160;&#160;Upon payment of such lump sum, all of Mr. Carlson&#8217;s outstanding options were canceled, terminated and returned to the plan pool.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Separation Agreement contains a general release by Mr. Carlson of all claims against the Company and its affiliates, a reaffirmation of Mr. Carlson&#8217;s obligations under any confidentiality, trade secrets or proprietary information and inventions assignment agreements or undertakings that he has signed with the Company (including the confidentiality and inventions assignment provisions of the Employment Agreement), as well as a reaffirmation of Mr. Carlson&#8217;s obligation under the Employment Agreement not to solicit or recommend for employment any person employed by the Company or its affiliates for a period of 18 months following the Carlson Effective Date.&#160;&#160;Mr. Carlson has also agreed to cooperate with the Company for the indefinite future in connection with certain pending litigation and other business matters in exchange for an hourly fee.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Letter of Credit Agreements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Litigation</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On January 7, 2010, ZO Skin Health, Inc., a California corporation, filed a complaint in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles: ZO Skin Health, Inc. vs. OMP, Inc. and Obagi Medical Products, Inc. and Does 1-25; Case No. BC429414.&#160;&#160;The complaint alleged claims against the Company for: (i) unfair competition; (ii) intentional interference with prospective economic advantage; (iii) negligent interference with prospective economic advantage; (iv) intentional interference with contract; and (v) promissory estoppel.&#160;&#160;More specifically, the plaintiff alleged that: the Company engaged in business practices, including the assertion of void and unlawful non-compete clauses in contracts with Zein Obagi, that violate California&#8217;s Unfair Competition Law and the California Business and Professional Code, Section 17200, et seq.; the Company intentionally and negligently interfered with plaintiff&#8217;s prospective economic advantage in relationship with Rohto and certain product distributors; the Company interfered with existing contracts between plaintiff and Rohto; and the Company allegedly did not provide certain promised assistance in connection with the alleged agreement between plaintiff and Rohto.&#160;&#160;The plaintiff sought injunctive relief, compensatory damages &#8220;measuring in the tens of millions of dollars&#8221; and other damages in an unspecified amount, punitive damages and costs of suit, including attorneys&#8217; fees.&#160;&#160;The Company answered the complaint and denied the allegations in that pleading.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company asserted counterclaims against the plaintiff.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, on or about January 7, 2010, Zein Obagi and his spouse, Samar Obagi, and the Zein and Samar Obagi Family Trust and certain other entities allegedly affiliated with Zein Obagi sent the Company an arbitration demand before JAMS (formerly Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services) in Los Angeles, California in which the claimants claimed breaches of the 2006 Services Agreement and 2006 Separation and Release Agreement between the Company and the claimants and various breaches of common law, California law, and federal law, including failure to pay certain retainer, marketing and reimbursement funds, failure to pay royalties allegedly due, failure to consult before developing and marketing new products, failure to pursue certain business strategies, threatening to invoke unenforceable and inapposite non-competition clauses in the Company&#8217;s contracts with Zein Obagi, threatening and interfering with the claimants&#8217; business opportunities, threatening to enforce nonexistent trademark and service mark rights, and wrongfully depriving the claimants of both their rights to pursue business opportunities and also their trademark rights.&#160;&#160;Claimants sought actual and consequential damages of tens of &#8220;millions of dollars&#8221; and other damages in an unspecified amount, restitution of monies wrongfully obtained in an unspecified amount, prejudgment interest, attorneys&#8217; fees and costs, declaratory judgment and assignment of certain trademarks from the Company to Dr. Obagi.&#160;&#160;The Company filed an answer to the Demand for Arbitration denying the allegations and asserting various counterclaims.&#160;&#160;In May 2010, the claimants in the arbitration proceeding filed an amended demand, again before JAMS in Los Angeles.&#160;&#160;The amended demand reiterated the claims asserted in the original demand.&#160;&#160;The amended demand expanded the original demand&#8217;s factual allegations involving the Company&#8217;s alleged interference with the claimants&#8217; rights to pursue business opportunities and with the claimants&#8217; trademark rights.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 2, 2011, the Company entered into the Settlement Agreement with the ZO Parties that resulted in the dismissal with prejudice of all claims and counterclaims in both the litigation and arbitration.&#160;&#160;Under the Settlement Agreement, the Company and ZO Parties have agreed to mutual releases.&#160;&#160;The Settlement Agreement also provides for: (i) a one-time payment of $5,000 from the Company to the ZO Parties; and (ii) the grant of a limited, non-exclusive license by the Company to the ZO Parties to use certain trademarks of the Company in up to three locations.&#160;&#160;In addition to the one-time settlement payment, the Company incurred legal costs related to the matter.&#160;&#160;The other non-economic terms of the Settlement Agreement are confidential.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded $5,000 for the one-time payment and $2,947 in related litigation fees as components of &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221; during the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The settlement was effective May 5, 2011 and the litigation and arbitration proceedings were dismissed with prejudice on May 10, 2011 and May 9, 2011, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From time to time, the Company is involved in other litigation and legal matters or disputes in the normal course of business.&#160;&#160;Individually and in the aggregate, management does not believe that the outcome of any of these other matters at this time, individually and in the aggregate, will have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;11: Stock Options</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2000, the Company adopted the 2000 Stock Option/Stock Issuance Plan (the &#8220;2000 Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The terms of the 2000 Plan provided for the grant of options to purchase common stock to employees, consultants, and directors.&#160;&#160;The 2000 Plan included incentive stock options (&#8220;ISOs&#8221;) and nonqualified stock options (&#8220;NSOs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The maximum number of shares of common stock that were allowed to be issued over the term of the 2000 Plan was not to exceed 375,000 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.&#160;&#160;In addition, the maximum number of shares of common stock issued to any person under the 2000 Plan in any calendar year was not to exceed 150,000 shares.&#160;&#160;In September 2001, the Board of Directors amended the 2000 Plan to increase the maximum number of shares of common stock that may be issued over the term of the 2000 Plan to 2,083,334 shares.&#160;&#160;The vesting period of options granted under this plan ranged from one to five years.&#160;&#160;Options expired within a period of not more than ten years from the grant date.&#160;&#160;In November 2005, the Board of Directors amended the 2000 Plan to discontinue further option grants under the plan.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011 and 2010, due to the aforementioned discontinuance of further option grants under the 2000 Plan, 280,590 and 273,815 shares are no longer available for the granting of additional options, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2005, the Company adopted the 2005 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2005 Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The 2005 Plan provides for the grant of ISOs and NSOs to employees, consultants and directors.&#160;&#160;On November&#160;27, 2006, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors amended the 2005 Plan.&#160;&#160;The amendments to the 2005 Plan included: (i)&#160;increasing the number of authorized shares to 1,500,000; (ii)&#160;establishing an evergreen clause that replenishes the 2005 Plan each year with a share amount equal to the lesser of 500,000<a name="eolPage82"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>&#160;shares, 3% of outstanding shares as of the preceding December 31, or such number of shares as is determined by the Board of Directors; (iii)&#160;and other administrative provisions.&#160;&#160;The amended 2005 Plan was approved by the stockholders of the Company on November&#160;28, 2006.&#160;&#160;On January&#160;9, 2007, February 27, 2008, and April 15, 2009, the Board of Directors replenished the 2005 Plan with 500,000 shares on each date, available for granting of additional options.&#160;&#160;In April 2010, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors further amended the 2005 Plan to: (i) eliminate the automatic share increase provision of the plan; (ii) provide that the authorized share reserve will be reduced by one share of the Company&#8217;s common stock for every one share subject to an option or stock appreciation right granted under the plan and one and one-half shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock for every one share subject to an award other than an option or stock appreciation right; (iii) extend the Company&#8217;s ability to grant certain performance-based awards under the plan; and (iv) effect various technical revisions. The amendment to the 2005 Plan, as previously amended, was approved by the stockholders of the Company at its 2010 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 8, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the 2005 Plan, the exercise price per share for both ISOs and NSOs shall not be less than 100% of the fair market value per share of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date.&#160;&#160;The exercise price per share for both ISOs and NSOs may not be less than 110% of the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date for an individual who, at the time of grant, owns stock representing more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all classes of the Company&#8217;s stock.&#160;&#160;The right to exercise the ISOs and the NSOs vests at a rate in accordance with the individual stock option agreements.&#160;&#160;The vesting period of the options granted under this plan typically ranges from three to five years.&#160;&#160;Options expire within a period of not more than ten years from the grant date.&#160;&#160;ISOs granted to an employee, who at the time of grant owns stock representing more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all classes of stock of the Company, expire within a period of not more than five years from the grant date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A total of 4,809,519 shares have been authorized for issuance under the 2000 Plan and the 2005 Plan (the &#8220;Plans&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Of the shares that have been authorized for issuance, 1,720,972 and 1,552,968 shares have been issued for options which have been exercised as of December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively, and 1,315,290 and 1,207,067 shares have been reserved for options that are outstanding as of December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011 and 2010, there were 1,298,207 and 1,647,254 shares available for granting of additional options, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><a name="FIS_UNIDENTIFIED_TABLE_34"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>Expected stock price volatility is based on a combined average expected stock price volatility of publicly traded peer companies deemed to be similar entities whose share or option prices are publicly available.&#160;&#160;For fiscal years 2011, 2010 and 2009 the Company based its expected stock price volatility on the combined average stock price volatility of five publicly traded peer companies.&#160;&#160;Until such time that the Company has enough historical data, it will continue to rely on peer companies&#8217; volatility and will ensure that the selected peer companies are still appropriate.&#160;&#160;The risk-free interest rate is based on the United States Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant with an equivalent remaining term.&#160;&#160;The Company does not currently plan to pay dividends in the near future.&#160;&#160;The Company has elected the simplified method for determining the expected life of options granted.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The aggregate intrinsic value of options outstanding for the year ended December 31, 2011 was $725, of which $293 related to vested options as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;This amount changes based on the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s stock.&#160;&#160;Aggregate intrinsic value represents the total pretax intrinsic value (the difference between the Company&#8217;s estimated stock price on December 31, 2011 and the exercise price, multiplied by the number of in-the-money options) that would have been received by the option holders had all the option holders exercised their options on December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;During the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, the Company recognized $1,307, $1,242 and $1,619, respectively, in stock-based compensation.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, the total unrecognized stock-based compensation expense related to nonvested stock options was approximately $2,093, which is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of approximately 2.26 years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, the Company issued a total of 16,045, 14,778 and 24,330 shares of restricted common stock, respectively, under the 2005 Plan to outside directors.&#160;&#160;The resulting compensation expense from the restricted stock grants is recognized on the straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which equals the restricted stock vesting term of one year.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the restricted stock granted during the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009 was $9.35, $12.18 and $7.40 per share, respectively, which was based upon the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The total fair value of restricted stock that vested during the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009 was $180, $180 and $165, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As discussed in Note 10, in connection with his appointment as President and Chief Executive Officer on April 21, 2011, the compensation committee awarded Mr. Hummel 50,000 RSUs, which also have a fair market value of $12.55 per share.&#160;&#160;The resulting compensation expense from the RSU grants is to be recognized on the straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which equaled the RSU vesting term of two years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Note&#160;12: Segments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block" align="left"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 280, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Segment Reporting,</font> requires that the Company disclose certain information about its operating segments where operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise about which separate financial information is available that is evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance.&#160;&#160;Generally, financial information is required to be reported on the basis that is used internally for evaluating segment performance and deciding how to allocate resources to segments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company operates its business on the basis of two reportable segments: (i)&#160;physician-dispensed; and (ii)&#160;licensing.&#160;&#160;The physician-dispensed segment produces a broad range of topical skin health systems and products that enable physicians to sell products to their patients to treat a range of skin conditions, including premature aging, photodamage, hyperpigmentation, acne, sun damage, facial redness and soft tissue deficits, such as fine lines and wrinkles.&#160;&#160;The licensing segment includes revenues generated from licensing arrangements with international distributors that specialize in the distribution and marketing of OTC medical oriented products in the drug store, retail and aesthetic spa channels.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February&#160;1, 1999, the Company established an employee savings and retirement plan and a 401(k) defined contribution retirement plan, covering substantially all full-time employees.&#160;&#160;Beginning April 2006, the Company matched 100% of employee contributions up to 2% of employee compensation.&#160;&#160;Effective January 1, 2008, the Company modified the 401(k) defined contribution retirement plan to match 100% of employee contributions up to 3% of employee compensation and 50% of employee contributions of the next 2% of employee compensation to a maximum of 4% of employee compensation.&#160;&#160;The Company may also make, at the discretion of the Board of Directors, additional contributions subject to statutory limits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>
